title: Compound V pre-eval record
description:
Canonical, write-once control-plane record written by the pre-eval scoring engine (A3) to docs/superpowers/pre-eval/<pre_eval_id>.json BEFORE any run dir exists (AC-2). `status: PRE_EVAL_DONE` is a RECORD field, NOT a state.json phase (AC-7/CR2-8) — there is no state.json at prediction time. `decision` carries one of three tiers (FASTPATH_ELIGIBLE / SCOPED_PIPELINE / FULL_PIPELINE, v3.0 spec §A1). Iron-Invariant #4 AS AMENDED (spec §A4): the score OFFERS by default and auto-routes only inside the DIRECT auto-route class, whose membership is decided by mechanically checkable predicates and never by model judgement; every other tier still requires a human offer and acceptance. Enforcement fields are deterministic (taxonomy/localization/override logic), never model magnitude (Iron-Invariant #1). C1's fast-path cross-artifact binding (AC-13) verifies pre_eval_id / decision / taxonomy_digest / localization-digest match across this record, the manifest, and the localization artifact.

DIGEST CONVENTION (CR5-6/CR5-7, single-sourced in compound-v-taxonomy.py, documented in docs/superpowers/architecture/pre-eval-config.md): the record's own `digest` = 'sha256:' + sha256(canonical_json(record MINUS the `digest` field)), where canonical_json = json.dumps(obj, sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':'), ensure_ascii=False, allow_nan=False). `taxonomy_digest` is a DISTINCT convention: 'sha256:' + sha256(RAW taxonomy-snapshot bytes) — a content address of the immutable snapshot, not a re-serialization.

then.description: ANY record that is not FULL_PIPELINE — FASTPATH_ELIGIBLE or SCOPED_PIPELINE — MUST pin a real, non-null taxonomy snapshot + its content-address. The condition is stated NEGATIVELY (`decision != FULL_PIPELINE`) on purpose: keyed on `const: FASTPATH_ELIGIBLE` it silently stopped applying the moment a third tier existed, and a SCOPED record with a null taxonomy would have validated — the exact fail-open this check exists to prevent. No proportionate tier is reachable without the sensitive-path + content-pattern protections: `_has_safety_coverage` in compound-v-preeval.py routes an absent, malformed or unreadable taxonomy to an unconditional FULL_PIPELINE, so this conditional is the machine-checked restatement of an engine invariant rather than a second policy. taxonomy_ref/taxonomy_digest are required and strictly typed here.

ANY FIRED OVERRIDE FORCES FULL (see also the taxonomy conditional above, which is keyed the same negative way) (v3.0 spec §A1). A record whose override_fired is a real row id MUST carry decision=FULL_PIPELINE. Machine-checked here so a record that pairs a hard override with a proportionate tier cannot exist even if a future producer regresses.

Tier agreement: `tier` is a readability alias for `decision`, never an independent claim. The triage gate prefers `tier`, so a disagreement would let a record be exempted as a tier its own decision refuses.
Tier agreement - see the FASTPATH_ELIGIBLE case above.

Tier agreement - see the FASTPATH_ELIGIBLE case above. This is the case that matters most: a FULL record wearing `tier: DIRECT` would be exempted by the triage gate as if it were the auto-route class.

SCOPED+ QUALIFIES SCOPED AND NOTHING ELSE (v3.4.1 §A3). `flavor: scoped_plus` obliges the run to carry a deep review job and a cross-model second opinion, which `--require-triage` then enforces on the manifest. On a FULL record that obligation is already exceeded and the flag is noise; on a FASTPATH_ELIGIBLE record it is a contradiction, since a DIRECT change has no manifest to put a review job in. Keyed on the PRESENCE of `flavor` rather than on its value, so a future flavor inherits the same pinning instead of quietly escaping it.

pre_eval_id.description: Write-once join key, minted before localization (CR5-10). Convention: 'YYYY-MM-DDThhmmssZ-<slug>-<nonce>'. The stream key for triage-outcomes and the binding key across every fast-path artifact. Independent of run_id (which does not exist yet).

run_id.description: The run this pre-eval later bound to, or null while unbound (a declined/full-pipeline request may never become a run). Set only via the `bind` triage event once the run dir is created; NEVER present at PRE_EVAL_DONE time.

request_slug.description: Slug derived from the request text (not the not-yet-existing plan). Human-readable; part of pre_eval_id.

ts.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp the record was written.

status.description: Record-status field (prose-only lifecycle token; AC-7/CR2-8). NOT a state.json phase — no run dir exists at prediction time.

taxonomy_version.description: The `version` of the taxonomy snapshot used. Human-readable; the machine binding is `taxonomy_digest`. NULL in the absent-taxonomy FULL_PIPELINE case (there is no taxonomy to version).

taxonomy_ref.description: Repo-relative, normalized, no-'..' path to the IMMUTABLE taxonomy snapshot the score was computed against (pre-run, under docs/superpowers/pre-eval/<pre_eval_id>.taxonomy-snapshot.yaml). A committed regular file (never an escaping symlink). Copied into the run preserving this digest when a fast-path materializes (CR2-6/CR4-2). NULLABLE for the absent-taxonomy case (see taxonomy_digest); the first `allOf` conditional (`if decision != FULL_PIPELINE`) makes it a required, non-null, non-empty string on any proportionate-tier record — FASTPATH_ELIGIBLE and SCOPED_PIPELINE alike.

taxonomy_digest.description: 'sha256:'+sha256(RAW snapshot bytes) of taxonomy_ref. On a FASTPATH_ELIGIBLE record it is required and MUST equal the manifest's taxonomy_digest (AC-13). ABSENT-TAXONOMY CASE (spec §2 missing-data table + Iron-Invariant #5): when the taxonomy file/snapshot is absent, malformed, or unavailable there is no snapshot to reference and no bytes to digest, so the engine STILL writes the record (and appends the `predicted` event) with decision=FULL_PIPELINE and `taxonomy_ref: null` / `taxonomy_digest: null` / `taxonomy_version: null`. Such a record validates precisely because these three fields are nullable when decision != FASTPATH_ELIGIBLE; the first `allOf` conditional forbids that null-taxonomy state from ever carrying a PROPORTIONATE decision — it is keyed `decision != FULL_PIPELINE`, so it binds SCOPED_PIPELINE exactly as it binds FASTPATH_ELIGIBLE. A3/C1/M1 MUST treat the null-taxonomy record as an unconditional FULL_PIPELINE. (`pattern` applies only when the value is a string, so null passes.)

tiers_signalled.description: Which evidence tiers produced a signal (audit trail + `confidence` evidence). NEVER a gating number.

override_fired.description: The Layer-A hard-override row id (1-7, spec §2 rows 1-6 plus the appended advisor-hot row 7) that forced FULL_PIPELINE, or null if none fired. A non-null value REQUIRES decision=FULL_PIPELINE, and the second `allOf` conditional above enforces it mechanically. This is not redundancy with the bands: override #4 (semantic-vs-path disagreement) records the GENUINE low/low bands beside override_fired=4, so a consumer that re-derived the tier from `difficulty`+`impact` would grant DIRECT — and with it the auto-route class — to a record whose own audit trail says a hard override fired. Read `decision`, never the bands.

decision.description: The triage outcome, one of THREE proportionate tiers (v3.0 spec §A1). FASTPATH_ELIGIBLE = tier DIRECT (implement in place, run the floor, commit on the branch — no manifest, no run dir); SCOPED_PIPELINE = tier SCOPED (manifest, run dir, scope gate, floor, one combined SPEC+QUALITY review; recon and the three pre-flights skipped); FULL_PIPELINE = tier FULL (the whole pipeline). The value is produced by the 3x3 difficulty×impact matrix INSIDE compound-v-preeval.py's `score`, and consumers MUST branch on all three values explicitly — a `== FASTPATH_ELIGIBLE ? A : B` reader is a two-value reader of a three-value enum. Iron-Invariant #4 AS AMENDED (spec §A4): the score OFFERS by default and auto-routes only inside the DIRECT auto-route class, whose membership is decided by mechanically checkable predicates and never by model judgement; every other tier still requires a human offer and acceptance. Any override / unknown axis / missing-or-malformed taxonomy / token-cap overrun ⇒ FULL_PIPELINE (fail-closed), and a non-null `override_fired` ALWAYS pairs with FULL_PIPELINE regardless of the recorded bands.

tier.description: OPTIONAL, and REDUNDANT BY CONSTRUCTION: the manifest-vocabulary token for `decision` (FASTPATH_ELIGIBLE=DIRECT, SCOPED_PIPELINE=SCOPED, FULL_PIPELINE=FULL - compound-v-preeval.py's DECISION_TO_TIER). The triage gate in `hooks/epic-goal-stop.sh` PREFERS this field over `decision` when it is present, so an unconstrained `tier` would be a second, higher-priority source of truth for a safety-relevant classification: a record could say `decision: FULL_PIPELINE` and `tier: DIRECT` and be exempted as DIRECT. The three tier-agreement conditionals in the top-level `allOf` therefore PIN it to `decision`, which makes the hook's preferred branch provably identical to its fallback rather than a way around it. Carry it for human readability; never as an independent claim. `decision` remains the authority.
tier.$comment: Pinned to `decision` by the tier-agreement conditionals in the top-level allOf.

flavor.description: OPTIONAL (v3.4.1 §A3). The SCOPED+ qualifier: a small, exactly-localized edit on a SENSITIVE path that a light classify called `plumbing` or `user-facing-minor`. It is deliberately NOT a fourth tier token — `decision` still carries one of three values and DECISION_TO_TIER still has three entries — because a fourth token would have to be taught to every consumer that branches on the tier. What it adds is an OBLIGATION on the run: a `type: review` job at `tier: deep` on `backend: claude`, plus a cross-model second opinion, plus the human accept. `compound-v-validate-manifest.py --require-triage` refuses a `scoped_plus` manifest that carries no such review job, which is what stops the flavor from being a label instead of a promise. Absent means ordinary SCOPED (or any other tier); the conditional in the top-level `allOf` pins its presence to decision=SCOPED_PIPELINE, so it can never qualify a FULL or DIRECT record.

t3_demotion.description: OPTIONAL (v3.4.1 §A2/§A3). What the TAXONOMY said, kept beside the decision a light classify was allowed to reach instead. The engine records it whenever T3 was consulted about the SIZE of a change (rather than about a path it could not band at all): `from` is the band pair T1 produced, `category` is the enum T3 answered, and `applied` says whether the demotion actually happened. IT IS EVIDENCE, NEVER A GATE: a reader that wants the tier reads `decision`. Its purpose is to make a demotion auditable after the fact — a record saying `from: {high, high}` beside `decision: SCOPED_PIPELINE` is the whole argument for that tier in one field, and a record saying `applied: false` is a change that asked to be small and was refused.

from.description: The bands T1 produced BEFORE the demotion — on §A2's path the broad glob's own bands, on §A3's the sensitive path's.

category.description: The T3 enum that was answered. Only `plumbing` and `user-facing-minor` ever demote; the other two are recorded with `applied: false`.

applied.description: Whether the bands were actually changed. False means T3 was asked and refused — the record keeps the question as well as the answer.

sensitive.description: Present and true on the §A3 (SCOPED+) path only: the demoted path is on the taxonomy's sensitive list. Absent on the ordinary §A2 broad-glob demotion.

t3_reason.description: OPTIONAL (v3.4.1). WHY the light classify was consulted: `unbanded` (T1 could not band the path at all — the pre-3.4.1 case), `demotion` (T1 banded it, but only from a broad directory glob, §A2), or `sensitive` (a small edit on a sensitive path that may reach SCOPED+, §A3). The re-entry is identical in all three cases, so nothing branches on this — it exists so a log or an audit can tell a classify that RESCUED a change from a broad glob apart from one that merely filled a gap.

session_id.description: The harness session this record was written in - the value on the `Stop` hook's stdin payload, compared EXACTLY by the triage gate in `hooks/epic-goal-stop.sh`. Written by `/v:triage`, the only component that knows it: the scoring engine never sees a session, so a record produced by `compound-v-preeval.py` alone omits this field. ABSENT OR NULL MEANS THE RECORD BINDS NO SESSION AND THEREFORE COVERS NOTHING - the gate's exact-match test cannot succeed against an empty value, which is the fail-closed direction. Never required: requiring it would invalidate every record the engine writes outside a triage command.
session_id.$comment: minLength applies only to the string form; null passes. The empty string is rejected because it asserts a session binding that can never match.

base_commit.description: The commit HEAD pointed at when this record was written. RECORDED, NOT DECISIVE: `hooks/epic-goal-stop.sh` reads it and deliberately derives NO freshness rule from it, because HEAD legitimately advances mid-session - any commit moves it, including /v:triage's own commit of this very record - so a mismatch is not evidence that the record is stale. The field exists so a human or a later audit can say which tree the classification was made against. Do not add a staleness check keyed on it without evidence that a mismatch actually correlates with a bad decision. (`pattern` applies only when the value is a string, so null passes.)

declared_paths.description: The repo-relative paths this record's classification actually covers - the field that turns the triage gate from an existence check into a COVERAGE check. `hooks/epic-goal-stop.sh` exempts a changed path only when the record is for the same session AND the path lies inside this set; without it, one triage of 'change the README' would exempt an unrelated later edit to that hook itself. COVERAGE IS THE THREE-WAY MATCH THAT HOOK IMPLEMENTS, and it is deliberately narrow: an exact string match, a DIRECTORY PREFIX only when the entry ends in `/`, or a glob only when the entry contains `*`. A bare `scripts` does NOT cover `scripts/app.py` - write `scripts/` or `scripts/**`. Widening a declared set by accident is the one direction this must not fail in, which is also why the item constraints reject what the hook would otherwise silently drop. Written by `/v:triage`; usually the localization's `resolved_paths`, but kept a separate field because a record may legitimately declare a broader set than triage resolved.

min_sample_status.description: Whether Tier-2 had >= min_sample_count calibrated FAST-PATH-TAKEN outcomes. `insufficient` (the launch default, no data) means Tier-2 is escalation-only (Iron-Invariant #3 counterfactual guard).

confidence.description: Evidence-only confidence label (signalled tiers + localization confidence). Shown as EVIDENCE, never a gating number (spec §2). Optional.

digest.description: Self-integrity digest of THIS record: 'sha256:'+sha256(canonical_json(record without `digest`)). Optional; when present, downstream verifies it with compound-v-taxonomy.record_digest(record, exclude_field='digest'). IT COVERS EVERY OTHER FIELD, the Feature-C binding (`session_id`, `base_commit`, `declared_paths`, `tier`) included. A producer that attaches the binding AFTER building the record ships one whose digest no longer verifies, and does so silently because this field is optional and only checked when present. Pass the binding to compound-v-preeval.py `build_record(..., binding={...})`, which folds it in before the digest is taken.

declared_path.description: One entry in `declared_paths`: a repo-relative path, a directory prefix (trailing `/`), or a glob (containing `*`). CONSTRAINED TO MATCH WHAT THE CONSUMER CAN ACTUALLY READ. `hooks/epic-goal-stop.sh` serializes candidates as `tierU+001Frun_idU+001Fpath` lines and DROPS any entry containing U+001F, LF or CR, because a re-escaped path would no longer equal the path git reports. Dropping narrows the declared set, which is the safe direction for the hook but silent for the producer - so this pattern rejects every C0 control character here, where the producer still learns. A leading `/` is rejected because paths are repo-relative and git never reports an absolute one, so such an entry could only ever match nothing while looking like coverage. `..` segments are rejected because an entry that escapes the repo cannot describe a changed path, and normalizing it here would create a second path semantics to keep in sync with the gate's.

band.description: A deterministic band — never a raw magnitude (Iron-Invariant #1). `unknown` forces FULL_PIPELINE via Layer-A override #6.

display.description: Derived 1-10 DISPLAY label (low→1-3, med→4-6, high→7-10); band-midpoint or per-tier max. Computed AFTER the decision — never the gate (spec §2).

localization.description: The bounded read-only localization result. When A1 writes it as the standalone committed artifact docs/superpowers/pre-eval/<pre_eval_id>.localization.json, that file has THIS shape and its own canonical-JSON `digest` (record_digest, exclude_field='digest'); that localization-digest is the value bound across manifest+record+artifact (AC-13).

resolved_paths.description: Repo-relative paths the request resolves to. Fast-path REQUIRES exactly one literal normalized path; resolved_paths[0] MUST equal the manifest's sole write_allowed literal (AC-13).

fan_out.description: How many distinct sites/paths the change touches. Fast-path requires fan_out <= pre_eval.fan_out_threshold (Layer-B).

flags.description: Semantic flags from the shared taxonomy classify() (e.g. sensitive_path, content:shared_token, content:a11y, content:feature_flag). Any override-triggering flag forces FULL_PIPELINE.

confidence.description: Localization confidence. `ambiguous`/`failed` ⇒ Layer-A override #1 ⇒ FULL_PIPELINE (Iron-Invariant #2: no `low` without exact localization). `new_file` (v3.4.1 §A4) is the fourth value: the request named ONE path that does not exist yet and whose parent directory does, so `resolved_paths` is that single path, `fan_out` is 1 and `flags` contains `new_file`. It is a LOCALIZED answer — override #1 does not fire and T1 still bands it from the directory's glob — but it is never DIRECT: the engine's Layer-B predicate tests `confidence == "exact"` by name, because a file nobody has read must not be committed with no manifest, no run dir and no review.
